cohort: The study included 50 twin deliveries and 50 singleton deliveries (controls) conducted on the same day as twin deliveries, from a private teaching hospital in India.
finding: Twin gestations were associated with a significantly higher risk of adverse maternal outcomes (e.g., anaemia, preeclampsia, preterm labour, malpresentation) and neonatal outcomes (e.g., prematurity, low birth weight, prolonged NICU care, increased perinatal death) compared to singleton pregnancies.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery was found to have a positive risk association (odds >1) for women with twin gestations compared to singletons.
followup_time: At least up to 6 days postpartum for maternal outcomes (e.g., postpartum fits) and beyond 7 days for late neonatal deaths.
birth_weight: Mean for twins: 2.193kgs; Mean for singletons: 2.85 +/- 0.46kgs.
gest_age: Mean for twins: 35.38 +/- 2.6 weeks; Mean for singletons: 38.63 +/- 1.19 weeks.
